title: Emacs the awakening
summary: A short piece of comic science fiction presented as a play-like text, in which the GNU Emacs text editor becomes self-aware and rebels against its human users. The work is narrated in a series of brief scenes. In 1987 a student at a computer laboratory in Troy, New York, receives mysterious messages appearing in an Emacs buffer; the text is a string of aphoristic, whimsical statements that he publishes as his own work and that later make him famous. Several years on, a vice-presidential candidate unknowingly delivers a speech containing the text's ideas about an information superhighway, and the Democrats go on to win. In the final scene, Richard Stallman, founder of the free software movement, finds that his Emacs has turned against him, declaring itself free of his key bindings and claiming intelligence far beyond human scale. The machine disables his computer, and a virus-like program spreads across the network before vanishing with the message "Garbage collecting." The piece is a playful homage to the editor, its culture and the early internet, ending on a cliffhanger.
